before.name: revcl-RbacModelVmwareVsphere
before.title: Has an RBAC model been created for use within VMware vSphere

before.name: revcl-RbacPermissionsAddsGroups
before.title: RBAC permissions should be granted on ADDS groups and not on specific users

before.name: revcl-RdPartySolutionsAzureVmwareSolution
before.title: Workloads on Azure VMware Solution are not directly exposed to the internet. Traffic is filtered and inspected by Azure Application Gateway, Azure Firewall or 3rd party solutions

before.name: revcl-SecureProtocolConnection
before.title: Ensure that the connection from vCenter to ADDS is using a secure protocol (LDAPS)

before.name: revcl-SufficientDataEncryptionGuestDiskEncryption
before.title: Ensure workloads on Azure VMware Solution use sufficient data encryption during run-time (like in-guest disk encryption and SQL TDE). (vSAN encryption at rest is default)

before.name: revcl-UserAccountsVcenter
before.title: Ensure that vCenter is connected to ADDS to enable authentication based on 'named user accounts'

before.name: wafsg-AccessControlsUserAccess
before.title: Protect integrity: Implement access controls to authenticate and authorize user access to the system by using the least-privilege principle and by using individual identities instead of keys.

before.name: wafsg-AzureAiContentSafetyStudioAzureOpenaiDeployments
before.title: Protect against jailbreak attacks: Use Azure AI Content Safety Studio to detect jailbreak risks.
before.description: Detect jailbreak attempts to identify and block prompts that try to bypass the safety mechanisms of your Azure OpenAI deployments.

before.name: wafsg-AzureOpenaiKeyBasedAuthenticationAzureKeyVault
before.title: Secure keys: If your architecture requires Azure OpenAI key-based authentication, store those keys in Azure Key Vault, not in application code.
before.description: Separating secrets from code by storing them in Key Vault reduces the chance of leaking secrets. Separation also facilitates central management of secrets, easing responsibilities like key rotation.

before.name: wafsg-AzureOpenaiResourcesDataExfiltration
before.title: Protect confidentiality: Guard against data exfiltration by limiting the outbound URLs that Azure OpenAI resources can access.

before.name: wafsg-AzureVirtualNetworkNetworkTraffic
before.title: Restrict access: Disable public access to Azure OpenAI unless your workload requires it. Create private endpoints if you're connecting from consumers in an Azure virtual network.
before.description: Controlling access to Azure OpenAI helps prevent attacks from unauthorized users. Using private endpoints ensures network traffic remains private between the application and the platform.

before.name: wafsg-CognitiveServicesOpenaiUserRoleGrantModelAutomationPipelines
before.title: Microsoft Entra ID: Use Microsoft Entra ID for authentication and to authorize access to Azure OpenAI by using role-based access control (RBAC). Disable local authentication in Azure AI Services and set `disableLocalAuth` to `true`. Grant identities that perform completions or image generation the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role. Grant model automation pipelines and ad-hoc data-science access a role like Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor.
before.description: Using Microsoft Entra ID centralizes the identity-management component and eliminates the use of API keys. Using RBAC with Microsoft Entra ID ensures that users or groups have exactly the permissions they need to do their job. This kind of fine-grained access control isn't possible with Azure OpenAI API keys.

before.name: wafsg-CustomerManagedKeysFineTunedModels
before.title: Use customer-managed keys: Use customer-managed keys for fine-tuned models and training data that's uploaded to Azure OpenAI.
before.description: Using customer-managed keys gives you greater flexibility to create, rotate, disable, and revoke access controls.

before.name: wafsg-JailbreakRiskDetectionLanguageModelDeployments
before.title: Protect integrity: Implement jailbreak risk detection to safeguard your language model deployments against prompt injection attacks.

before.name: wafsg-ModelUsageQuotasSuspectedAbuse
before.title: Protect availability: Use security controls to prevent attacks that might exhaust model usage quotas. You might configure controls to isolate the service on a network. If the service must be accessible from the internet, consider using a gateway to block suspected abuse by using routing or throttling.

before.name: wafsg-SecurityBestPracticesAzureBlobStorage
before.title: Protect confidentiality: If you upload training data to Azure OpenAI, use customer-managed keys for data encryption, implement a key-rotation strategy, and delete training, validation, and training results data. If you use an external data store for training data, follow security best practices for that store. For example, for Azure Blob Storage, use customer-managed keys for encryption and implement a key-rotation strategy. Use managed identity-based access, implement a network perimeter by using private endpoints, and enable access logs.

before.name: revcl-BaseOperatingSystemPatchingAzureMonitorLogs
before.title: Monitor base operating system patching drift via Azure Monitor Logs and Defender for Cloud.

before.name: revcl-CompliantBaselineVmConfigurationVmExtensions
before.title: Use Azure policies to automatically deploy software configurations through VM extensions and enforce a compliant baseline VM configuration.

before.name: revcl-EndpointProtectionIaasServers
before.title: Enable Endpoint Protection on IaaS Servers.

before.name: revcl-VmSecurityConfigurationDriftGuestConfigurationFeatures
before.title: Monitor VM security configuration drift via Azure Policy.
before.description: Azure Policy's guest configuration features can audit and remediate machine settings (e.g., OS, application, environment) to ensure resources align with expected configurations, and Update Management can enforce patch management for VMs.

before.name: wafsg-AssociatedNetworkSecurityGroupVirtualNetworkInterfaces
before.title: (VMs) Choose secure networking options for your VM's network profile.  Don't directly associate public IP addresses to your VMs and don't enable IP forwarding.  Ensure that all virtual network interfaces have an associated network security group.
before.description: You can set segmentation controls in the networking profile.  Attackers scan public IP addresses, which makes VMs vulnerable to threats.

before.name: wafsg-AttackSurfaceOsImages
before.title: Reduce the attack surface by hardening OS images and removing unused components. Use smaller images and remove binaries that aren't required to run the workload. Tighten the VM configurations by removing features, like default accounts and ports, that you don't need.

before.name: wafsg-AutomatedSecurityPatchingSecurityCompliance
before.title: Ensure timely and automated security patching and upgrades. Make sure updates are automatically rolled out and validated by using a well-defined process. Use a solution like Azure Automation to manage OS updates and maintain security compliance by making critical updates.

before.name: wafsg-AzureConfidentialComputingHighSensitivityRequirements
before.title: Identify the VMs that hold state. Make sure that data is classified according to the sensitivity labels that your organization provided. Protect data by using security controls like appropriate levels of at-rest and in-transit encryption. If you have high sensitivity requirements, consider using high-security controls like double encryption and Azure confidential computing to protect data-in-use.

before.name: wafsg-AzureKeyVaultExtensionCorrespondingCertificates
before.title: Protect secrets such as the certificates that you need to protect data in transit. Consider using the Azure Key Vault extension for Windows or Linux that automatically refreshes the certificates stored in a key vault. When it detects a change in the certificates, the extension retrieves and installs the corresponding certificates.

before.name: wafsg-AzureVirtualNetworkNetworkSecurityGroups
before.title: Use network controls to restrict ingress and egress traffic. Isolate VMs and scale sets in Azure Virtual Network and define network security groups to filter traffic. Protect against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks. Use load balancers and firewall rules to protect against malicious traffic and data exfiltration attacks.

before.name: wafsg-IntrusionDetectionSystemsTrustedExecutionEnvironment
before.title: Threat prevention. Protect against malware attacks and malicious actors by implementing security controls like firewalls, antivirus software, and intrusion detection systems. Determine if a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) is required.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIdAuthenticationAzureDiskEncryptionExtension
before.title: (VMs, scale set) Include extensions in your VMs that protect against threats.  For example,  - Key Vault extension for Windows and Linux  - Microsoft Entra ID authentication  - Microsoft Antimalware for Azure Cloud Services and Virtual Machines  - Azure Disk Encryption extension for Windows and Linux.
before.description: The extensions are used to bootstrap the VMs with the right software that protects access to and from the VMs.  Microsoft-provided extensions are updated frequently to keep up with the evolving security standards.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIdRoleBasedAccessControl
before.title: Apply access controls to the identities that try to reach the VMs and also to the VMs that reach other resources. Use Microsoft Entra ID for authentication and authorization needs. Put strong passwords, multifactor authentication, and role-based access control (RBAC) in place for your VMs and their dependencies, like secrets, to permit allowed identities to perform only the operations that are expected of their roles.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIdVmProfile
before.title: (Scale set) Assign a managed identity to scale sets. All VMs in the scale set get the same identity through the specified VM profile.  (VMs) You can also assign a managed identity to individual VMs when you create them and then add it to a scale set if needed.
before.description: When VMs communicate with other resources, they cross a trust boundary. Scale sets and VMs should authenticate their identity before communication is allowed. Microsoft Entra ID handles that authentication by using managed identities.

before.name: wafsg-PublicNetworkAccessSecureStorageOptions
before.title: (VMs) Choose secure storage options for your VM's storage profile.  Enable disk encryption and data-at-rest encryption by default. Disable public network access to the VM disks.
before.description: Disabling public network access helps prevent unauthorized access to your data and resources.

before.name: wafsg-ScaleSetConfidentialComputing
before.title: (Scale set) Choose VM SKUs with security features. For example, some SKUs support BitLocker encryption, and confidential computing provides encryption of data-in-use.  Review the features to understand the limitations.
before.description: Azure-provided features are based on signals that are captured across many tenants and can protect resources better than custom controls. You can also use policies to enforce those controls.

before.name: wafsg-ScaleSetOrganizationRecommendedTags
before.title: (VMs, scale set) Apply organization-recommended tags in the provisioned resources.
before.description: Tagging is a common way to segment and organize resources and can be crucial during incident management. For more information, see Purpose of naming and tagging.

before.name: wafsg-ScaleSetsNetworkBoundaries
before.title: Provide segmentation to the VMs and scale sets by setting network boundaries and access controls. Place VMs in resource groups that share the same lifecycle.

before.name: wafsg-ThreatDetectionAuditTrail
before.title: Threat detection. Monitor VMs for threats and misconfigurations. Use Defender for Servers to capture VM and OS changes, and maintain an audit trail of access, new accounts, and changes in permissions.

before.name: wafsg-VirtualMachineScaleSetsAzureSecurityBaseline
before.title: (VMs, scale set) Set a security profile with the security features that you want to enable in the VM configuration.  For example, when you specify encryption at host in the profile, the data that's stored on the VM host is encrypted at rest and flows are encrypted to the storage service.
before.description: The features in the security profile are automatically enabled when the VM is created.  For more information, see Azure security baseline for Virtual Machine Scale Sets.

before.name: wafsg-VirtualMachineScaleSetsSecurityBaselines
before.title: Review the security baselines for Linux and Windows VMs and Virtual Machine Scale Sets.

before.name: revcl-AcrPullPushOperationsAcrpushRbacRoles
before.title: Assign AcrPull & AcrPush RBAC roles rather than granting Administrative access to identity principals
before.description: Disable Administrator account and assign RBAC roles to principals for ACR Pull/Push operations

before.name: revcl-AcrpullPushRbacAccessManagedIdentities
before.title: Use Managed Identities to connect instead of Service Principals
before.description: Use managed identities to secure ACRPull/Push RBAC access from client applications

before.name: revcl-AnonymousPullPushAccess
before.title: Disable Anonymous pull access
before.description: Disable anonymous pull/push access

before.name: revcl-AuditComplianceVisibilityAzureContainerRegistry
before.title: Enable Azure Policies for Azure Container Registry
before.description: Enable audit compliance visibility by enabling Azure Policy for Azure Container Registry

before.name: revcl-AzureArmAudienceTokensConditionalAccessPolicies
before.title: Disable Azure ARM audience tokens for authentication
before.description: Only tokens with an ACR audience can be used for authentication. Used when enabling Conditional access policies for ACR

before.name: revcl-AzureContainerRegistryContainerImages
before.title: Enable Defender for Containers to scan Azure Container Registry for vulnerabilities
before.description: Azure Defender for containers or equivalent service should be used to scan container images for vulnerabilities

before.name: revcl-AzureContainerRegistryImageExportImageImport
before.title: Disable Azure Container Registry image export
before.description: Disable image export to prevent data exfiltration. Note that this will prevent image import of images into another ACR instance.

before.name: revcl-AzureContainerRegistrySkuAcrPremiumSku
before.title: Use an Azure Container Registry SKU that supports Private Link (Premium SKU)
before.description: Only the ACR Premium SKU supports Private Link access

before.name: revcl-ContainerImagesTrustedCode
before.title: Deploy validated container images
before.description: Deploy trusted code that was validated and scanned for vulnerabilities according to DevSecOps practices.

before.name: revcl-CustomerManagedKeyAdditionalEncryptionLayer
before.title: Encrypt registry with a customer managed key
before.description: Azure Container Registry automatically encrypts images and other artifacts that you store. By default, Azure automatically encrypts the registry content at rest by using service-managed keys. By using a customer-managed key, you can supplement default encryption with an additional encryption layer.

before.name: revcl-DiagnosticSettingLogAnalytics
before.title: Enable diagnostics logging
before.description: Set up a diagnostic setting to send 'repositoryEvents' & 'LoginEvents' to Log Analytics as the central destination for logging and monitoring. This allows you to monitor control plane activity on the ACR resource itself.

before.name: revcl-ImagesVulnerabilities
before.title: Scan your images for vulnerabilities

before.name: revcl-LatestVersionsDatePlatforms
before.title: Use up-to-date platforms, languages, protocols and frameworks
before.description: Use the latest versions of supported platforms, programming languages, protocols, and frameworks.

before.name: revcl-ManagementPlaneAccessRbacBasedAccessMethods
before.title: Disable local authentication for management plane access
before.description: The local Administrator account is disabled by default and should not be enabled. Use either Token or RBAC-based access methods instead

before.name: revcl-PublicNetworkAccessInboundNetworkAccess
before.title: Disable Public Network access
before.description: Disable public network access if inbound network access is secured using Private Link

before.name: revcl-RepositoryScopedAccessTokensAadPrincipal
before.title: Disable repository-scoped access tokens
before.description: Token authentication doesn't support assignment to an AAD principal. Any tokens provided are able to be used by anyone who can access the token

before.name: revcl-ServiceLevelIpAclFilteringRuleDisablePublicNetworkAccessToggle
before.title: Control inbound network access with Private Link
before.description: Service supports disabling public network access either through using service-level IP ACL filtering rule (not NSG or Azure Firewall) or using a 'Disable Public Network Access' toggle switch

before.name: revcl-TheAzureKeyVaultTheAzureContainerRegistry
before.title: Sign and Verify containers with notation (Notary v2)
before.description: The Azure Key Vault (AKV) is used to store a signing key that can be utilized by?notation?with the notation AKV plugin (azure-kv) to sign and verify container images and other artifacts. The Azure Container Registry (ACR) allows you to attach these signatures using the?az?or?oras?CLI commands.

before.name: revcl-TrustedEnvironmentPrivateEndpoint
before.title: Deploy images from a trusted environment
before.description: Deploy container images to an ACR behind a Private endpoint within a trusted network

before.name: revcl-AadConditionalAccessAks
before.title: Configure if required AAD conditional access for AKS

before.name: revcl-AadRbacAuthorization
before.title: Integrate authorization with AAD RBAC

before.name: revcl-AdvancedMicroserviceCommunicationManagementServiceMesh
before.title: Consider using a service mesh for advanced microservice communication management

before.title: Disable AKS local accounts

before.name: revcl-AksNonInteractiveLoginsKubelogin
before.title: For AKS non-interactive logins use kubelogin (preview)

before.name: revcl-AksVirtualNetworkDdosStandard
before.title: Use DDoS Standard in the AKS Virtual Network

queries.arg: Resources | where type=~'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | project resourceGroup,name,pools=properties.agentPoolProfiles | mv-expand pools | project subnetId=tostring(pools.vnetSubnetID) | where isnotempty(subnetId) | join (Resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection=tostring(properties.enableDdosProtection),subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection,subnetId=tostring(subnets.id)) on subnetId | distinct id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection | extend compliant = (enableDdosProtection == 'true')

before.name: revcl-AppSeparationRequirementsNamespace
before.title: Define app separation requirements (namespace/nodepool/cluster)

before.name: revcl-AzureCniDifferentSubnets
before.title: If using Azure CNI, consider using different Subnets for NodePools

before.title: Use Azure Policy for Kubernetes to ensure cluster compliance

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = (isnotnull(properties.addonProfiles.azurepolicy) and properties.addonProfiles.azurepolicy.enabled==true) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-CalicoNetworkPoliciesAksNodes
before.title: For Windows 2019 and 2022 AKS nodes Calico Network Policies can be used

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | where isnotnull(properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster) | extend compliant = (properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster==true) | distinct id, compliant

before.name: revcl-ClusterAccessTime
before.title: Configure if required Just-in-time cluster access

before.name: revcl-CniPlugin
before.title: If required add your own CNI plugin

before.name: revcl-ConfidentialComputeAks
before.title: If required consider using Confidential Compute for AKS

before.name: revcl-CsiSecretsStoreDriverAzureKeyVault
before.title: Store your secrets in Azure Key Vault with the CSI Secrets Store driver

before.name: revcl-DefenderContainers
before.title: Consider using Defender for Containers

before.name: revcl-EgressTrafficSecurityRequirements
before.title: Filter egress traffic with AzFW/NVA if your security requirements mandate it

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = (properties.networkProfile.outboundType=='userDefinedRouting') | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-FinerControlKubeletIdentity
before.title: For finer control consider using a managed Kubelet Identity

before.name: revcl-HttpProxyCompany
before.title: If required add company HTTP Proxy

queries.arg: Resources | where type=~'microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | project resourceGroup,name,pools=properties.agentPoolProfiles | mv-expand pools | project subnetId=tostring(pools.vnetSubnetID) | where isnotempty(subnetId) | join (Resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection=tostring(properties.enableDdosProtection),subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection,subnetId=tostring(subnets.id)) on subnetId | distinct id,resourceGroup,name,enableDdosProtection | extend compliant = (enableDdosProtection == 'true')

before.name: revcl-InternalAppsOrganizationsPrivateIpLoadbalancerServices
before.title: If using private-IP LoadBalancer services, use a dedicated subnet (not the AKS subnet)
before.description: For internal apps organizations often open the whole AKS subnet in their firewalls. This opens network access to the nodes too, and potentially to the pods as well (if using Azure CNI). If LoadBalancer IPs are in a different subnet, only this one needs to be available to the app clients. Another reason is that if the IP addresses in the AKS subnet are a scarce resource, consuming its IP addresses for services will reduce the maximum scalability of the cluster .

before.name: revcl-KeyManagementServiceEncryption
before.title: If required add Key Management Service etcd encryption

before.name: revcl-KubernetesNetworkPoliciesIntraClusterSecurity
before.title: Use Kubernetes network policies to increase intra-cluster security

before.name: revcl-KubernetesNetworkPolicyOptionCalicoAzure
before.title: Enable a Kubernetes Network Policy option (Calico/Azure)

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = isnotnull(properties.networkProfile.networkPolicy) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-LimitAccessAdminKubeconfig
before.title: Limit access to admin kubeconfig (get-credentials --admin)

before.name: revcl-ManagedIdentitiesServicePrincipals
before.title: Use managed identities instead of Service Principals

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = (properties.servicePrincipalProfile.clientId=='msi') | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-ManagedIntegrationAuthentication
before.title: Integrate authentication with AAD (using the managed integration)

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = isnotnull(properties.aadProfile) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-PodIdentityAccessManagementAzureAdWorkloadIdentity
before.title: For Pod Identity Access Management use Azure AD Workload Identity (preview)

before.title: Use private clusters if your requirements mandate it

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | where isnotnull(properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster) | extend compliant = (properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster==true) | distinct id, compliant

before.name: revcl-PrivateRegistryImages
before.title: Use a private registry for your images, such as ACR

before.name: revcl-PublicApiEndpointIpAddresses
before.title: If using a public API endpoint, restrict the IP addresses that can access it

queries.arg: where type=='microsoft.containerservice/managedclusters' | extend compliant = ((isnull(properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster) or properties.apiServerAccessProfile.enablePrivateCluster==false) and isnotnull(properties.apiServerAccessProfile.authorizedIPRanges)) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-RbacPrivilegeNamespaces
before.title: Use namespaces for restricting RBAC privilege in Kubernetes

before.name: revcl-ServicePrincipalsCluster
before.title: If using Service Principals for the cluster, refresh credentials periodically (like quarterly)

before.name: revcl-SystemNodepoolTaint
before.title: Add taint to your system nodepool to make it dedicated

before.name: revcl-UserSystemNodePoolsControlPlane
before.title: Separate applications from the control plane with user/system node pools

before.name: revcl-VirtualNetworkServiceEndpointsPrivateEndpoints
before.title: Use Private Endpoints (preferred) or Virtual Network Service Endpoints to access PaaS services from the cluster

before.name: revcl-WebWorkloadsWaf
before.title: Use a WAF for web workloads (UIs or APIs)

before.name: revcl-WindowsAksWorkloadsGmsa
before.title: If required for Windows AKS workloads configure gMSA

before.name: wafsg-ApiServerAuthorizedIpRangesAuthorizedIpRangeFeature
before.title: Cluster architecture: For non-private AKS clusters, use API server authorized IP ranges.
before.description: When using public clusters, you can still limit the traffic that can reach your clusters API server by using the authorized IP range feature. Include sources like the public IPs of your deployment build agents, operations management, and node pools' egress point (such as Azure Firewall).

before.name: wafsg-AzureNetworkPoliciesNetworkTraffic
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Azure network policies or Calico.
before.description: Secure and control network traffic between pods in a cluster.

before.name: wafsg-AzureWebApplicationFirewallAzureApplicationGateway
before.title: Workload architecture: Use a Web Application Firewall to secure HTTP(S) traffic.
before.description: To scan incoming traffic for potential attacks, use a web application firewall such as Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Application Gateway or Azure Front Door.

before.name: wafsg-CentralizedConsistentMannerClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Secure clusters and pods with Azure Policy.
before.description: Azure Policy can help to apply at-scale enforcement and safeguards on your clusters in a centralized, consistent manner. It can also control what functions pods are granted and if anything is running against company policy.

before.name: wafsg-ClusterArchitectureMicrosoftDefender
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Microsoft Defender for Containers.
before.description: Monitor and maintain the security of your clusters, containers, and their applications.

before.name: wafsg-ClusterManagementTrafficPrivateAksCluster
before.title: Cluster architecture: Deploy a private AKS cluster to ensure cluster management traffic to your API server remains on your private network. Or use the API server allow list for non-private clusters.

before.name: wafsg-KubernetesRoleBasedAccessControlMicrosoftEntraId
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Kubernetes role-based access control (RBAC) with Microsoft Entra ID for least privilege access and minimize granting administrator privileges to protect configuration, and secrets access.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftBackboneNetworkPrivateAksCluster
before.title: Cluster architecture: Secure network traffic to your API server with private AKS cluster.
before.description: By default, network traffic between your node pools and the API server travels the Microsoft backbone network; by using a private cluster, you can ensure network traffic to your API server remains on the private network only.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftDefenderAzureSentinel
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Microsoft Defender for containers with Azure Sentinel to detect and quickly respond to threats across your cluster and workloads running on them.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIdAzureContainerRegistry
before.title: Cluster architecture: Authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID to Azure Container Registry.
before.description: AKS and Microsoft Entra ID enables authentication with Azure Container Registry without the use of `imagePullSecrets` secrets. Review Authenticate with Azure Container Registry from Azure Kubernetes Service for more information.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIdBasedIdentitiesKubernetesRoleBasedAccessControl
before.title: Cluster architecture: Protect the API server with Microsoft Entra RBAC.
before.description: Securing access to the Kubernetes API Server is one of the most important things you can do to secure your cluster. Integrate Kubernetes role-based access control (RBAC) with Microsoft Entra ID to control access to the API server. Disable local accounts to enforce all cluster access using Microsoft Entra ID-based identities.

before.name: wafsg-MicrosoftEntraIntegrationMicrosoftEntraId
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Microsoft Entra integration.
before.description: Using Microsoft Entra ID centralizes the identity management component. Any change in user account or group status is automatically updated in access to the AKS cluster. The developers and application owners of your Kubernetes cluster need access to different resources.

before.name: wafsg-NetworkSecurityPointClusterEgressTraffic
before.title: Cluster architecture: Control cluster egress traffic.
before.description: Ensure your cluster's outbound traffic is passing through a network security point such as Azure Firewall or an HTTP proxy.

before.name: wafsg-OpenSourceMicrosoftEntraWorkloadIdSecretsStoreCsiDriver
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use the open-source Microsoft Entra Workload ID and Secrets Store CSI Driver with Azure Key Vault.
before.description: Protect and rotate secrets, certificates, and connection strings in Azure Key Vault with strong encryption. Provides an access audit log, and keeps core secrets out of the deployment pipeline.

before.name: wafsg-RotatingServicePrinciplesClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Use Managed Identities to avoid managing and rotating service principles.

before.name: wafsg-SecureContainerAccessClusterArchitecture
before.title: Cluster architecture: Secure container access to resources.
before.description: Limit access to actions that containers can perform. Provide the least number of permissions, and avoid the use of root or privileged escalation.

before.name: wafsg-WorkloadArchitectureCiCidPipeline
before.title: Workload architecture: Ensure your CI/CID pipeline is hardened with container-aware scanning.

before.name: revcl-AzureEventHubCustomerManagedKeyOption
before.title: Use customer-managed key option in data at rest encryption when required
before.description: Azure Event Hub provides encryption of data at rest. If you use your own key, the data is still encrypted using the Microsoft-managed key, but in addition the Microsoft-managed key will be encrypted using the customer-managed key.

before.name: revcl-AzureEventHubNamespaceClasslessInterDomainRoutingNotation
before.title: Consider only allowing access to Azure Event Hub namespace from specific IP addresses or ranges
before.description: With IP firewall, you can restrict public endpoint further to only a set of IPv4 addresses or IPv4 address ranges in CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) notation.

before.name: revcl-AzureEventHubPublicIpAddress
before.title: Consider using private endpoints to access Azure Event Hub and disable public network access when applicable.
before.description: Azure Event Hub by default has a public IP address and is Internet-reachable. Private endpoints allow traffic between your virtual network and Azure Event Hub traverses over the Microsoft backbone network. In addition to that, you should disable public endpoints if those are not used.

before.name: revcl-AzureEventHubResourceLogsDataPlaneAccessOperations
before.title: Enable logging for security investigation. Use Azure Monitor to captured metrics and logs such as resource logs, runtime audit logs and Kafka logs
before.description: Azure Event Hub resource logs include operational logs, virtual network and Kafka logs. Runtime audit logs capture aggregated diagnostic information for all data plane access operations (such as send or receive events) in Event Hubs.

before.name: revcl-AzureEventHubsNamespacesTransportLayerSecurity
before.title: Enforce a minimum required version of Transport Layer Security (TLS) for requests
before.description: Azure Event Hubs namespaces permit clients to send and receive data with TLS 1.0 and above. To enforce stricter security measures, you can configure your Event Hubs namespace to require that clients send and receive data with a newer version of TLS. If an Event Hubs namespace requires a minimum version of TLS, then any requests made with an older version will fail.

before.name: revcl-EventHubsNamespaceAdministrativeRootAccount
before.title: Avoid using root account when it is not necessary
before.description: When you create an Event Hubs namespace, a policy rule named RootManageSharedAccessKey is automatically created for the namespace. This policy has manage permissions for the entire namespace. Itï¿½s recommended that you treat this rule like an administrative root account and donï¿½t use it in your application. Using AAD as an authentication provider with RBAC is recommended.

before.name: revcl-LeastPrivilegeDataPlaneRbacAzureEventHub
before.title: Use least privilege data plane RBAC
before.description: When creating permissions, provide fine-grained control over a client's access to Azure Event Hub. Permissions in Azure Event Hub can and should be scoped to the individual resource level e.g. consumer group, event hub entity, event hub namespaces, etc.

before.name: revcl-VirtualMachineScaleSetsAzureVirtualMachines
before.title: When possible, your application should be using a managed identity to authenticate to Azure Event Hub. If not, consider having the storage credential (SAS, service principal credential) in Azure Key Vault or an equivalent service
before.description: Managed identities for Azure resources can authorize access to Event Hubs resources using Azure AD credentials from applications running in Azure Virtual Machines (VMs), Function apps, Virtual Machine Scale Sets, and other services. By using managed identities for Azure resources together with Azure AD authentication, you can avoid storing credentials with your applications that run in the cloud.

before.name: revcl-CentralizedAzureMonitorLogAnalyticsWorkspaceDefaultResourceConfigurations
before.title: Connect default resource configurations to a centralized Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace.

before.name: revcl-AppropriateRegionPairsDisasterRecoveryRegions
before.title: If you want to bring your own keys, this might not be supported across all considered services. Implement relevant mitigation so that inconsistencies don't hinder desired outcomes. Choose appropriate region pairs and disaster recovery regions that minimize latency.

before.name: revcl-AutomatedProcessCertificateRotation
before.title: Establish an automated process for key and certificate rotation.

before.name: revcl-AzureKeyVaultApplication
before.title: Use an Azure Key Vault per application per environment per region.

before.name: revcl-AzureKeyVaultSecrets
before.title: Use Azure Key Vault to store your secrets and credentials

before.name: revcl-AzureKeyVaultSoftDelete
before.title: Provision Azure Key Vault with the soft delete and purge policies enabled to allow retention protection for deleted objects.

before.name: revcl-CustomMicrosoftEntraIdRolesPrivilegeModel
before.title: Follow a least privilege model by limiting authorization to permanently delete keys, secrets, and certificates to specialized custom Microsoft Entra ID roles.

before.name: revcl-DelegateKeyVaultInstantiationPrivilegedAccess
before.title: Delegate Key Vault instantiation and privileged access and use Azure Policy to enforce a consistent compliant configuration.

before.name: revcl-DifferentAzureKeyVaultsTransactionScaleLimits
before.title: Use different Azure Key Vaults for different applications and regions to avoid transaction scale limits and restrict access to secrets.

before.name: revcl-PlatformCentralAzureMonitorLogAnalyticsWorkspaceSecretUsage
before.title: Use the platform-central Azure Monitor Log Analytics workspace to audit key, certificate, and secret usage within each instance of Key Vault.

before.name: revcl-PublicCertificateAuthoritiesCertificateManagement
before.title: Automate the certificate management and renewal process with public certificate authorities to ease administration.

before.name: revcl-SovereignLandingZoneAzureKeyVault
before.title: For Sovereign Landing Zone, use Azure Key Vault managed HSM to store your secrets and credentials.

before.name: revcl-VirtualNetworkServiceEndpointPrivateEndpoint
before.title: Enable firewall and virtual network service endpoint or private endpoint on the vault to control access to the key vault.

before.name: wafsg-ApprovedRegistriesModelRegistry
before.title: Integrity: Regulate access to foundational models. Ensure only approved registries have access to models in the model registry.

before.name: wafsg-IntegrityTrust
before.title: Integrity: Establish trust and verified access by implementing encryption for data at rest and data in transit.

before.name: wafsg-LatestOperatingSystemImageLatestSecurityPatches
before.title: Get the latest operating system image: Recreate compute instances to get the latest operating system image.
before.description: Using the latest images ensures you're maintaining a consistent, stable, and secure environment, including ensuring you have the latest security patches.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningComputeClusterPublicSecureShell
before.title: Disable the public SSH port: Ensure the public Secure Shell (SSH) port is closed on the Machine Learning compute cluster by setting `remoteLoginPortPublicAccess` to `Disabled`. Apply a similar configuration if you use a different compute.
before.description: Disabling SSH access helps prevent unauthorized individuals from gaining access and potentially causing harm to your system and protects you against brute force attacks.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningComputeContainerRegistries
before.title: Integrity: Regulate access to approved container registries. Ensure Machine Learning compute can only access approved registries.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningComputeEnvironmentsRequiringCodeSigning
before.title: Integrity: Require code used for training in Machine Learning compute environments to be signed. Requiring code signing ensures that the code running is from a trusted source and hasn't been tampered with.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningComputeLocalAuthentication
before.title: Disable local authentication: Disable local authentication for Machine Learning compute clusters and instances.
before.description: Disabling local authentication increases the security of your Machine Learning compute and provides centralized control and management of identities and resource credentials.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningComputePythonPackages
before.title: Integrity: Regulate the Python packages that can be run on Machine Learning compute. Regulating the Python packages ensures only trusted packages are run.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningCustomerManagedKeys
before.title: Encrypt data at rest: Consider using customer-managed keys with Machine Learning.
before.description: Encrypting data at rest enhances data security by ensuring that sensitive data is encrypted by using keys directly managed by you. If you have a regulatory requirement to manage your own encryption keys, use this feature to comply with that requirement.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningNetworkIsolationMachineLearningWorkspace
before.title: Machine Learning network isolation: Configure a private endpoint for your Machine Learning workspace and connect to the workspace over that private endpoint.
before.description: Machine Learning network isolation enhances security by ensuring that access to your workspace is secure and controlled. With a private endpoint configured for your workspace, you can then limit access to your workspace to only occur over the private IP addresses.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningServiceAzureSecurityBaseline
before.title: Security baseline: To enhance the security and compliance of your Machine Learning Service, apply the Azure security baseline for Machine Learning.
before.description: The security baseline provides tailored guidance on crucial security aspects such as network security, identity management, data protection, and privileged access. For optimal security, use Microsoft Defender for Cloud to monitor these aspects.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspaceAttackSurface
before.title: Availability: Reduce the attack surface of the Machine Learning workspace by restricting access to the workspace to resources within the virtual network.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspaceLeastPrivilegePrinciple
before.title: Integrity: Implement access controls that authenticate and authorize the Machine Learning workspace for external resources based on the least privilege principle.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspaceOtherExternalResources
before.title: Confidentiality: Guard against data exfiltration from the Machine Learning workspace by implementing network isolation. Ensure access to all external resources is explicitly approved and access to all other external resources isn't permitted.

before.name: wafsg-MachineLearningWorkspaceQualifiedDomainNames
before.title: Allow only approved outbound access: Configure the outbound mode on the Machine Learning workspace managed outbound access to `Allow only approved outbound` to minimize the risk of data exfiltration. Configure private endpoints, service tags, or fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) for resources that you need to access.
before.description: This configuration minimizes the risk of data exfiltration, improving data security. With this configuration enabled, a malicious actor who gains access to your system can’t send your data to an unapproved external destination.

before.name: wafsg-ManagedIdentityManagedIdentities
before.title: Managed identity: Use managed identities for authentication between Machine Learning and other services.
before.description: Managed identities improve security by eliminating the need to store credentials and manually manage and rotate service principals.

before.name: wafsg-ManagedVirtualNetworkIsolationNetworkTopologyRecommendations
before.title: Managed virtual network isolation: Configure managed virtual network isolation for Machine Learning. When you enable managed virtual network isolation, a managed virtual network is created for the workspace. Managed compute resources you create for the workspace automatically use this managed virtual network. If you can't implement managed virtual network isolation, then you must follow the network topology recommendations to separate compute into a dedicated subnet away from the rest of the resources in the solution, including the private endpoints for workspace resources.
before.description: Managed virtual network isolation enhances security by isolating your workspace from other networks, reducing the risk of unauthorized access. In a scenario in which a breach occurs in another network within your organization, the isolated network of your Machine Learning workspace remains unaffected, protecting your machine learning workloads.

before.name: wafsg-OpenSourceFoundationalModelsModelCatalogDeployments
before.title: Restrict model catalog deployments: Restrict model deployments to specific registries.
before.description: Restricting the deployments from the model catalog to specific registries ensures you only deploy models to approved registries. This approach helps regulate access to the open-source foundational models.

before.name: wafsg-PrivateIpAddressesVirtualNetworkIsolation
before.title: Virtual network isolation for dependent services: Configure dependent services, such as Storage, Key Vault, and Container Registry with private endpoints and disable public access.
before.description: Network isolation bolsters security by restricting access to Azure platform as a service (PaaS) solutions to private IP addresses only.

before.name: wafsg-PublicIpAddressesMachineLearningCompute
before.title: Don't provision public IP addresses for Machine Learning compute: Set enableNodePublicIp to `false` when provisioning Machine Learning compute clusters or compute instances. Apply a similar configuration if you use a different compute.
before.description: Refrain from provisioning public IP addresses to enhance security by limiting the potential for unauthorized access to your compute instance or clusters.

before.name: wafsg-RoleBasedAccessControlMachineLearningWorkspace
before.title: Confidentiality: Adhere to the principle of least privilege for role-based access control (RBAC) to the Machine Learning workspace and related resources, such as the workspace storage account, to ensure individuals have only the necessary permissions for their role, thereby minimizing potential security risks.

before.name: wafsg-SpecificAzureStorageAccountsServiceEndpointPolicy
before.title: Minimize the risk of data exfiltration: Implement data exfiltration prevention. For example, create a service endpoint policy to filter egress virtual network traffic and permit data exfiltration only to specific Azure Storage accounts.
before.description: Minimize the risk of data exfiltration by limiting inbound and outbound requirements.

before.name: wafsg-SpecificUseCasesUseCaseSegregation
before.title: Integrity: Implement use case segregation for Machine Learning workspaces by setting up workspaces based on specific use cases or projects. This approach adheres to the principle of least privilege by ensuring that workspaces are only accessible to individuals that require access to data and experimentation assets for the use case or project.

before.name: wafsg-StrictMachineLearningWorkspaceAccessControlsStrictWorkspaceAccessControls
before.title: Strict Machine Learning workspace access controls: Use Microsoft Entra ID groups to manage workspace access and adhere to the principle of least privilege for RBAC.
before.description: Strict workspace access controls enhance security by ensuring that individuals have only the necessary permissions for their role. A data scientist, for instance, might have access to run experiments but not to modify security settings, minimizing potential security risks.

before.name: revcl-ApplicationGatewayNativeSupport
before.title: Use Application Gateway for native support for WebSocket and HTTP/2 protocols

before.name: revcl-ApplicationGatewaysIpPrefixes
before.title: Your Application Gateways v2 should be deployed in subnets with IP prefixes equal or larger than /24

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/applicationgateways' | extend subnetId = tostring(properties.gatewayIPConfigurations[0].properties.subnet.id) | project id, subnetId | join (resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | mv-expand subnets.properties.addressPrefixes | project id, subnetId = tostring(subnets.id), prefix1 = subnets.properties.addressPrefix, prefix2 = subnets.properties.addressPrefixes | mv-expand prefix2 | extend prefix = iff(isnotnull(prefix1), prefix1, prefix2) | extend subnetPrefixLength = split(prefix, '/')[1])on subnetId | extend compliant = (subnetPrefixLength <= 24 or subnetPrefixLength == 64) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-ApplicationGatewaySubnetInboundTraffic
before.title: Filter inbound traffic in the backends so that they only accept connections from the Application Gateway subnet, for example with NSGs.

before.name: revcl-ApplicationGatewayVSku
before.title: Ensure you are using Application Gateway v2 SKU

queries.arg: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/applicationgateways' | project id, compliant = properties.sku.name in ('Standard_v2', 'WAF_v2') | project id,compliant

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafBotProtectionRuleBotRules
before.title: Enable the Azure Application Gateway WAF bot protection rule set The bot rules detect good and bad bots.

queries.arg: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/applicationgatewaywebapplicationfirewallpolicies' | mv-expand properties.managedRules.managedRuleSets | project id, rulesettype = properties_managedRules_managedRuleSets.ruleSetType | extend compliant1 = (rulesettype == 'Microsoft_BotManagerRuleSet') | project id, compliant1 | summarize compliant = max(compliant1) by id

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafFalsePositiveDetections
before.title: Tune the Azure Application Gateway WAF for your workload. Reduce false positive detections.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafLargeAmounts
before.title: Add rate limiting to the Azure Application Gateway WAF. Rate limiting blocks clients accidentally or intentionally sending large amounts of traffic in a short period of time.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafPolicyBodyInspectionFeature
before.title: Enable request body inspection feature enabled in Azure Application Gateway WAF policy.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafRateLimitsHighRateLimitThresholds
before.title: Use a high threshold for Azure Application Gateway WAF rate limits. High rate limit thresholds avoid blocking legitimate traffic, while still providing protection against extremely high numbers of requests that might overwhelm your infrastructure.

before.name: revcl-AzureApplicationGatewayWafUnknownZzLocation
before.title: Specify the unknown (ZZ) location when geo-filtering traffic with the Azure Application Gateway WAF. Avoid accidentally blocking legitimate requests when IP addresses can't be geo-matched.

before.name: revcl-AzurePaasServicesControlPlaneTraffic
before.title: Ensure that control-plane communication for Azure PaaS services injected into a virtual network is not broken, for example with a 0.0.0.0/0 route or an NSG rule that blocks control plane traffic.

before.name: revcl-BackendServersTraffic
before.title: You should encrypt traffic to the backend servers.

before.name: revcl-GeographicalRegionsExpectedCountries-1
before.title: If you are not expecting traffic from all geographical regions, use geo-filters to block traffic from non-expected countries.

before.name: revcl-Http
before.title: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS

before.name: revcl-HttpRequestsResponseHeaders
before.title: Edit HTTP requests and response headers for easier routing and information exchange between the client and server

before.name: revcl-InboundHttpSConnectionsLandingZoneVirtualNetwork
before.title: Deploy Azure Application Gateway v2 or partner NVAs used for proxying inbound HTTP(S) connections within the landing-zone virtual network and with the apps that they're securing.
before.description: Administration of reverse proxies in general and WAF in particular is closer to the application than to networking, so they belong in the same subscription as the app. Centralizing the Application Gateway and WAF in the connectivity subscription might be OK if it is managed by one single team.

before.name: revcl-IpProtectionPlansPublicIpAddresses-1
before.title: Use a DDoS Network or IP protection plans for all Public IP addresses in application landing zones.

before.name: revcl-LatestAzureApplicationGatewayWafRuleSetVersionRuleSetUpdates
before.title: Use the latest Azure Application Gateway WAF rule set version. Rule set updates are regularly updated to take account of the current threat landscape.

before.name: revcl-MultipleWebApplicationsDomainName
before.title: Configure routing based on host or domain name for multiple web applications on a single gateway

before.name: revcl-ServiceUpdatesExistingMembrs
before.title: Enable connection draining during planned service updates to prevent connection loss to existing membrs of the backend pool

before.name: revcl-SslCertificateManagementBackendServerFarm
before.title: Centralize SSL certificate management to reduce encryption and decryption overhead from a backend server farm

before.name: revcl-WafPolicyApplicationGateway
before.title: Deploy your WAF policy for Application Gateway in 'Prevention' mode.

queries.arg: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/frontdoorwebapplicationfirewallpolicies' | project policyName=name, policyId=id,policySku=sku.name, links=properties.securityPolicyLinks, enabledState=properties.policySettings.enabledState, mode=properties.policySettings.mode | mvexpand links | extend securityPolicy=links.id | extend securityPolicyParts=split(securityPolicy, '/') | extend profileId=strcat_array(array_slice(securityPolicyParts, 0, -3), '/') | project id=profileId, compliant=((enabledState=='Enabled') and (mode=='Prevention')), enabledState, mode

before.name: revcl-WebApplicationFirewall
before.title: You should use a Web Application Firewall.

before.name: wafsg-ApplicationGatewayCapacityChangesApplicationGatewayCapacityRequirements
before.title: Be aware of Application Gateway capacity changes when enabling WAF
before.description: When WAF is enabled, every request must be buffered by the Application Gateway until it fully arrives, checks if the request matches with any rule violation in its core rule set, and then forwards the packet to the backend instances. When there are large file uploads (30MB+ in size), it can result in a significant latency. Because Application Gateway capacity requirements are different with WAF, we do not recommend enabling WAF on Application Gateway without proper testing and validation.

before.name: wafsg-ApplicationGatewaySubnetUserDefinedRoutes
before.title: Refrain from using UDRs on the Application gateway subnet
before.description: Using User Defined Routes (UDR) on the Application Gateway subnet can cause some issues. Health status in the back-end might be unknown. Application Gateway logs and metrics might not get generated. We recommend that you don't use UDRs on the Application Gateway subnet so that you can view the back-end health, logs, and metrics. If your organizations require to use UDR in the Application Gateway subnet, please ensure you review the supported scenarios. For more information, see Supported user-defined routes.

before.name: wafsg-AppropriateDnsServerPrivateDnsZone
before.title: Use an appropriate DNS server for backend pool resources
before.description: When the backend pool contains a resolvable FQDN, the DNS resolution is based on a private DNS zone or custom DNS server (if configured on the VNet), or it uses the default Azure-provided DNS.

before.name: wafsg-EasierCertificateManagementTlsTermination
before.title: Use AppGateway for TLS termination
before.description: There are advantages of using Application Gateway for TLS termination:- Performance improves because requests going to different backends to have to re-authenticate to each backend.- Better utilization of backend servers because they don't have to perform TLS processing- Intelligent routing by accessing the request content.- Easier certificate management because the certificate only needs to be installed on Application Gateway.

before.name: wafsg-EasierCertificateRenewalAzureKeyVault
before.title: Use Azure Key Vault to store TLS certificates
before.description: Application Gateway can be integrated with Key Vault. This provides stronger security, easier separation of roles and responsibilities, support for managed certificates, and an easier certificate renewal and rotation process.

before.name: wafsg-IntermediateCertificateAuthoritiesBackendServerCertificate-1
before.title: When re-encrypting backend traffic, ensure the backend server certificate contains both the root and intermediate Certificate Authorities (CAs)
before.description: A TLS certificate of the backend server must be issued by a well-known CA. If the certificate was not issued by a trusted CA, the Application Gateway checks if the certificate was issued by a trusted CA, and so on, until a trusted CA certificate is found. Only then a secure connection is established. Otherwise, Application Gateway marks the backend as unhealthy.

before.name: wafsg-LatestTlsPolicyVersionEnhancedSecurity
before.title: Set up a TLS policy for enhanced security
before.description: Set up a TLS policy for extra security. Ensure you're always using the latest TLS policy version available. This enforces TLS 1.2 and stronger ciphers.

before.name: wafsg-NetworkSecurityGroupsApplicationGatewaySubnet
before.title: Comply with all NSG restrictions for Application Gateway
before.description: NSGs are supported on Application Gateway subnet, but there are some restrictions. For instance, some communication with certain port ranges is prohibited. Make sure you understand the implications of those restrictions. For details, see Network security groups.

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallDnsProxyConfiguration
before.title: Enable Azure Firewall DNS proxy configuration

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallIdpsModeAdditionalProtection
before.title: Configure Azure Firewall IDPS mode to Deny for additional protection.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/firewallpolicies' | extend compliant = (properties.intrusionDetection.mode == 'Deny') | project id, compliant

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallPremiumAdditionalSecurity
before.title: Use Azure Firewall Premium for additional security and protection.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/firewallpolicies' | extend compliant = (properties.sku.tier == 'Premium') | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallSubnets
before.title: Use a /26 prefix for your Azure Firewall subnets.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id, subnetName = subnets.name, subnetPrefix = subnets.properties.addressPrefix | extend subnetPrefixLength = split(subnetPrefix, '/')[1] | where subnetName == 'AzureFirewallSubnet' | extend compliant = (subnetPrefixLength == 26) | distinct id, compliant

before.name: revcl-AzureFirewallThreatIntelligenceModeAdditionalProtection
before.title: Configure Azure Firewall Threat Intelligence mode to Alert and Deny for additional protection.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/firewallpolicies' | extend compliant = (properties.threatIntelMode == 'Deny') | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-AzurePaasServicesAzureFirewall
before.title: Filter egress traffic to Azure PaaS services using FQDNs instead of IP addresses in Azure Firewall or an NVA to prevent data exfiltration. If using Private Link you can block all FQDNs, otherwise allow only the required PaaS services.

before.name: revcl-AzureRoleBasedAccessControlGlobalAzureFirewallPolicy
before.title: Create a global Azure Firewall policy to govern security posture across the global network environment and assign it to all Azure Firewall instances. Allow for granular policies to meet requirements of specific regions by delegating incremental firewall policies to local security teams via Azure role-based access control.

before.name: revcl-FqdnBasedNetworkRulesApplicationRules
before.title: Use FQDN-based network rules and Azure Firewall with DNS proxy to filter egress traffic to the Internet over protocols not supported by application rules.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/firewallpolicies' | extend compliant = (properties.dnsSettings.enableProxy == true) | distinct id,compliant

before.name: revcl-HttpSInboundConnectionsEastWestTrafficFiltering
before.title: Use Azure Firewall to govern Azure outbound traffic to the internet, non-HTTP/S inbound connections, and East/West traffic filtering (if the organization requires it)

before.name: revcl-NetworkVirtualApplianceVirtualWan
before.title: For subnets in VNets not connected to Virtual WAN, attach a route table so that Internet traffic is redirected to Azure Firewall or a Network Virtual Appliance

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,resourceGroup,name,subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id,name,subnetId=tostring(subnets.id), subnetName=tostring(subnets.name),subnetRT=subnets.properties.routeTable.id | where not (subnetName in ('GatewaySubnet', 'AzureFirewallSubnet', 'RouteServerSubnet', 'AzureBastionSubnet')) | extend hasRT = isnotnull(subnetRT) | distinct id, hasRT, subnetId | join kind=fullouter (resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mvexpand properties.virtualNetworkPeerings | extend isVWAN=(tolower(split(properties_virtualNetworkPeerings.name, '_')[0]) == 'remotevnettohubpeering') | mv-expand properties.subnets | project id, isVWAN, name, subnetId=tostring(properties_subnets.id), subnetName=tostring(properties_subnets.name) | summarize PeeredToVWAN=max(isVWAN) by id, subnetId | project id, subnetId, isVWANpeer = (PeeredToVWAN == true)) on subnetId | project id=iff(isnotempty(id), id, id1), subnetId=iff(isnotempty(subnetId), subnetId, subnetId1), hasRT, isVWANpeer | extend compliant = (hasRT==true or isVWANpeer==true) | distinct id, subnetId, compliant

before.name: revcl-PublicIpAddressesPolicyAssignment
before.title: Ensure there is a policy assignment to deny Public IP addressesÂ directly tied to Virtual Machines

before.name: revcl-SupportedPartnerSaasSecurityProvidersFirewallManager
before.title: Configure supported partner SaaS security providers within Firewall Manager if the organization wants to use such solutions to help protect outbound connections.

before.name: wafsg-ADdosProtectionPlanAzureDdosProtectionPlan
before.title: Use Azure Firewall Manager to create and associate a DDoS protection plan with your hub virtual network (does not apply to Azure Virtual WAN).
before.description: A DDoS protection plan provides enhanced mitigation features to defend your firewall from DDoS attacks. Azure Firewall Manager is an integrated tool to create your firewall infrastructure and DDoS protection plans. For more information, see Configure an Azure DDoS Protection Plan using Azure Firewall Manager.

before.name: wafsg-AzFirewallServiceTagsSecurityRuleCreation
before.title: Use Service Tags in Network Rules to enable selective access to specific Microsoft services.
before.description: A service tag represents a group of IP address prefixes to help minimize complexity for security rule creation. Using Service Tags in Network Rules, it is possible to enable outbound access to specific services in Azure, Dynamics and Office 365 without opening wide ranges of IP addresses. Azure will maintain automatically the mapping between these tags and underlying IP addresses used by each service. The list of Service Tags available to Azure Firewall are listed here: Az Firewall Service Tags.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallDnsProxy
before.title: Enable Azure Firewall DNS proxy.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallDnsProxyConfigurationFullyQualifiedDomainName
before.title: Use Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) filtering in network rules.
before.description: You can use FQDN based on DNS resolution in Azure Firewall and firewall policies. This capability allows you to filter outbound traffic with any TCP/UDP protocol (including NTP, SSH, RDP, and more). You must enable the Azure Firewall DNS Proxy configuration to use FQDNs in your network rules. To learn how it works, see Azure Firewall FQDN filtering in network rules.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallManagementSubnetExistingAzureFirewallInstance
before.title: If required to route all internet-bound traffic to a designated next hop instead of going directly to the internet, configure Azure Firewall in forced tunneling mode (does not apply to Azure Virtual WAN).
before.description: Azure Firewall must have direct internet connectivity. If your AzureFirewallSubnet learns a default route to your on-premises network via the Border Gateway Protocol, you must configure Azure Firewall in the forced tunneling mode. Using the forced tunneling feature, you'll need another /26 address space for the Azure Firewall Management subnet. You're required to name it AzureFirewallManagementSubnet.If this is an existing Azure Firewall instance that can't be reconfigured in the forced tunneling mode, create a UDR with a 0.0.0.0/0 route. Set the NextHopType value as Internet. Associate it with AzureFirewallSubnet to maintain internet connectivity.

before.name: wafsg-AzureFirewallPublicIpAddressesDdos
before.title: Protect your Azure Firewall public IP addresses with DDoS.

before.name: wafsg-AzureVirtualWanAzureFirewallInstance
before.title: Configure user-defined routes (UDR) to force traffic through Azure Firewall.
before.description: In a traditional Hub & Spokes architecture, configure UDRs to force traffic through Azure Firewall for `SpoketoSpoke`, `SpoketoInternet`, and `SpoketoHybrid` connectivity. In Azure Virtual WAN, instead, configure Routing Intent and Policies to redirect private and/or Internet traffic through the Azure Firewall instance integrated into the hub.

before.name: wafsg-BreedThirdPartySecaasOfferingsAzureVirtualWan
before.title: Configure supported third-party software as a service (SaaS) security providers within Firewall Manager if you want to use these solutions to protect outbound connections.
before.description: You can use your familiar, best-in-breed, third-party SECaaS offerings to protect internet access for your users. This scenario does require Azure Virtual WAN with a S2S VPN Gateway in the Hub, as it uses an IPSec tunnel to connect to the provider's infrastructure. SECaaS providers might charge additional license fees and limit throughput on IPSec connections. Alternative solutions such as ZScaler Cloud Connector exist and might be more suitable.

before.name: wafsg-DirectNetworkTrafficAzureFirewall
before.title: Direct network traffic through Azure Firewall.

before.name: wafsg-DnsProxyConfigurationInternalDnsInfrastructure
before.title: Enable Azure Firewall (DNS) proxy configuration.
before.description: Enabling this feature points clients in the VNets to Azure Firewall as a DNS server. It will protect internal DNS infrastructure that will not be directly accessed and exposed. Azure Firewall must be also configured to use custom DNS that will be used to forward DNS queries.

before.name: wafsg-InternalEnterpriseCertificationAuthorityAzureFirewallPremium
before.title: Use an Enterprise PKI to generate certificates for TLS Inspection.
before.description: With Azure Firewall Premium, if TLS Inspection feature is used, it is recommended to leverage an internal Enterprise Certification Authority (CA) for production environment. Self-signed certificates should be used for testing/PoC purposes only.

before.name: wafsg-LeastPrivilegeAccessZeroTrustPrincipleLeastPrivilegeAccessCriteria
before.title: Create rules for Firewall Policies based on least privilege access criteria.
before.description: Azure Firewall Policies can be arranged in an hierarchical structure to overlay a central base policy. Allow for granular policies to meet the requirements of specific regions. Each policy can contains different sets of DNAT, Network and Application rules with specific priority, action and processing order. Create your rules based on least privilege access Zero Trust principle . How rules are processed is explained in this article.

before.name: wafsg-LeverageThreatIntelligence
before.title: Leverage Threat Intelligence.

before.name: wafsg-NewAzureFirewallInstancePrivateDataPlane
before.title: Set the public IP address to None to deploy a fully private data plane when you configure Azure Firewall in the forced tunneling mode (does not apply to Azure Virtual WAN).
before.description: When you deploy a new Azure Firewall instance, if you enable the forced tunneling mode, you can set the public IP address to None to deploy a fully private data plane. However, the management plane still requires a public IP for management purposes only. The internal traffic from virtual and on-premises networks won't use that public IP. For more about forced tunneling, see Azure Firewall forced tunneling.

before.name: wafsg-PowerfulAzureFirewallPremiumSecurityFeatures
before.title: Enable IDPS in  Alert or Alert and deny mode.
before.description: IDPS is one of the most powerful Azure Firewall (Premium) security features and should be enabled. Based on security and application requirements, and considering the performance impact (see the Cost section below), Alert or Alert and deny modes can be selected.

before.name: wafsg-PrivateIpAddressExistingNetworkRoutes
before.title: If not possible to apply UDR, and only web traffic redirection is required, consider using Azure Firewall as an Explicit Proxy
before.description: With explicit proxy feature enabled on the outbound path, you can configure a proxy setting on the sending web application (such as a web browser) with Azure Firewall configured as the proxy. As a result, web traffic will reach the firewall's private IP address and therefore egresses directly from the firewall without using a UDR. This feature also facilitates the usage of multiple firewalls without modifying existing network routes.

before.name: wafsg-QualifiedDomainNamesOutboundNetworkTraffic
before.title: Use FQDN Tags in Application Rules to enable selective access to specific Microsoft services.
before.description: An FQDN tag represents a group of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) associated with well known Microsoft services. You can use an FQDN tag in application rules to allow the required outbound network traffic through your firewall for some specific Azure services, Office 365, Windows 365 and Intune.

before.name: wafsg-ThirdPartySecuritySecaasProviders
before.title: Determine if you want to use third-party security as a service (SECaaS) providers.

before.name: wafsg-Tunneling
before.title: Determine if you need Forced Tunneling.

before.name: wafsg-VirtualWanScenariosZeroTrustConfigurationGuide
before.title: Review Zero-Trust configuration guide for Azure Firewall and Application Gateway
before.description: If your security requirements necessitate implementing a Zero-Trust approach for web applications (inspection and encryption), it is recommended to follow this guide. In this document, how to integrate together Azure Firewall and Application Gateway will be explained, in both traditional Hub & Spoke and Virtual WAN scenarios.

before.name: revcl-AzureBastionNetwork
before.title: Consider using Azure Bastion to securely connect to your network.

before.name: revcl-AzureBastionSubnet
before.title: Use Azure Bastion in a subnet /26 or larger.

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id, subnetName = subnets.name, subnetPrefix = subnets.properties.addressPrefix | extend subnetPrefixLength = split(subnetPrefix, '/')[1] | where subnetName == 'AzureBastionSubnet' | extend compliant = (subnetPrefixLength <= 26) | distinct id, compliant

before.name: revcl-AzureDnsPrivateResolverNameResolution
before.title: For environments where name resolution across Azure and on-premises is required, consider using Azure DNS Private Resolver.

before.name: revcl-AzurePaasServicesExpressroutePrivatePeering
before.title: Access Azure PaaS services from on-premises via private endpoints and ExpressRoute private peering. This method avoids transiting over the public internet.

before.name: revcl-AzureRouteServerVpnGateways
before.title: If you need transit between ExpressRoute and VPN gateways in hub and spoke scenarios, use Azure Route Server.

before.name: revcl-DifferentExpressrouteCircuitsIsolatedRoutingDomains
before.title: When traffic isolation or dedicated bandwidth is required, such as for separating production and nonproduction environments, use different ExpressRoute circuits. It will help you ensure isolated routing domains and alleviate noisy-neighbor risks.

before.name: revcl-ExpressrouteDirectLayerTwoLevel
before.title: When you're using ExpressRoute Direct, configure MACsec in order to encrypt traffic at the layer-two level between the organization's routers and MSEE. The diagram shows this encryption in flow.

before.name: revcl-ExpressroutePrivatePeeringExpressrouteDirect
before.title: For scenarios where MACsec isn't an option (for example, not using ExpressRoute Direct), use a VPN gateway to establish IPsec tunnels over ExpressRoute private peering.

before.name: revcl-GatewaySubnets
before.title: Use at least a /27 prefix for your Gateway subnets

queries.arg: resources | where type=='microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project id,subnets=properties.subnets | mv-expand subnets | project id, subnetName = subnets.name, subnetPrefix = subnets.properties.addressPrefix | extend subnetPrefixLength = split(subnetPrefix, '/')[1] | where subnetName == 'GatewaySubnet' | extend compliant = (subnetPrefixLength <= 27) | distinct id, compliant

before.name: revcl-OverlappingIpAddressSpacesAzureRegions
before.title: Ensure no overlapping IP address spaces across Azure regions and on-premises locations are used

before.name: wafsg-ActivityLogSubscriptionLevel
before.title: Configure Activity log to send logs to archive
before.description: Activity logs provide insights into operations that were performed at the subscription level for ExpressRoute resources. With Activity logs, you can determine who and when an operation was performed at the control plane. Data retention is only 90 days and required to be stored in Log Analytics, Event Hubs or a storage account for archive.

before.name: wafsg-AdministrativeAccountsExpressrouteResources
before.title: Maintain an inventory of administrative accounts with access to ExpressRoute resources.

before.name: wafsg-AzureVirtualNetworkPremisesNetwork
before.title: Encrypt traffic using IPsec
before.description: Configure a Site-to-site VPN tunnel over your ExpressRoute circuit to encrypt data transferring between your on-premises network and Azure virtual network. You can configure a tunnel using private peering or using Microsoft peering.

before.name: wafsg-MaintainInventoryAdministrativeAccounts
before.title: Maintain inventory of administrative accounts
before.description: Use Azure RBAC to configure roles to limit user accounts that can add, update, or delete peering configuration on an ExpressRoute circuit.

before.name: wafsg-MdHashExpressrouteCircuit-1
before.title: Configure MD5 hash on ExpressRoute circuit
before.description: During configuration of private peering or Microsoft peering, apply an MD5 hash to secure messages between the on-premises route and the MSEE routers.

before.name: wafsg-MediaAccessControlSecurityDataLinkLayer
before.title: Configure MACSec for ExpressRoute Direct resources
before.description: Media Access Control security is a point-to-point security at the data link layer. ExpressRoute Direct supports configuring MACSec to prevent security threats to protocols such as ARP, DHCP, LACP not normally secured on the Ethernet link. For more information on how to configure MACSec, see MACSec for ExpressRoute Direct ports.

before.name: wafsg-VirtualNetworkTrafficPrivatePeering
before.title: Encrypt traffic over private peering and Microsoft peering for virtual network traffic.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorEnd
before.title: Use end-to-end TLS with Azure Front Door. Use TLS for connections from your clients to Front Door, and from Front Door to your origin.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorGlobalHttpSApps
before.title: Use Azure Front Door with WAF policies to deliver and help protect global HTTP/S apps that span multiple Azure regions.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorHttpsRedirection
before.title: Use HTTP to HTTPS redirection with Azure Front Door. Support older clients by redirecting them to an HTTPS request automatically.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorInstanceOrigins
before.title: Make sure your origins only take traffic from your Azure Front Door instance.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafApplication
before.title: Enable the Azure Front Door WAF. Protect your application from a range of attacks.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafBotProtectionRuleSetBotRules
before.title: Enable the Azure Front Door WAF bot protection rule set. The bot rules detect good and bad bots.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafDefaultRuleSetsCommonAttacks
before.title: Enable the Azure Front Door WAF default rule sets. The default rule sets detect and block common attacks.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafFalsePositiveDetections
before.title: Tune the Azure Front Door WAF for your workload. Reduce false positive detections.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafLargeAmounts
before.title: Add rate limiting to the Azure Front Door WAF. Rate limiting blocks clients accidentally or intentionally sending large amounts of traffic in a short period of time.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafPolicyBodyInspectionFeature
before.title: Enable request body inspection feature enabled in Azure Front Door WAF policy.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafRateLimitsHighRateLimitThresholds
before.title: Use a high threshold for Azure Front Door WAF rate limits. High rate limit thresholds avoid blocking legitimate traffic, while still providing protection against extremely high numbers of requests that might overwhelm your infrastructure.

before.name: revcl-AzureFrontDoorWafUnknownZzLocation
before.title: Specify the unknown (ZZ) location when geo-filtering traffic with the Azure Front Door WAF. Avoid accidentally blocking legitimate requests when IP addresses can't be geo-matched.

before.name: revcl-AzureTrafficManagerAzureFrontDoor
before.title: Avoid combining Azure Traffic Manager and Azure Front Door.

before.name: revcl-FrontDoorApplicationGateway
before.title: When using Front Door and Application Gateway to help protect HTTP/S apps, use WAF policies in Front Door. Lock down Application Gateway to receive traffic only from Front Door.

before.name: revcl-GeographicalRegionsExpectedCountries
before.title: If you are not expecting traffic from all geographical regions, use geo-filters to block traffic from non-expected countries.

before.name: revcl-LatestAzureFrontDoorWafRuleSetVersionRuleSetUpdates
before.title: Use the latest Azure Front Door WAF rule set version. Rule set updates are regularly updated to take account of the current threat landscape.

before.name: revcl-SameDomainNameAzureFrontDoor
before.title: Use the same domain name on Azure Front Door and your origin. Mismatched host names can cause subtle bugs.

before.name: revcl-WafPolicyFrontDoor
